messages.subject: Differential analysis question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Meena and all MSstats developers,
First, thanks for the great series of webinars. I wanted to try the MSstats, again, to include this in our workflows and I came across a potential problem.
Doing the differential analysis with different software I get a lot of discrepancies and also strange results from MSstats.

Why are the p-values so strangely aligned on the line? This analysis was done with the Progenesis output. I also used a package SafeQuant https://github.com/eahrne/SafeQuant on the same dataset and I get something completely different.

I understand that these are different tests: linear model Vs (The summarized peptide/protein expression values are used for statistical testing of between condition differentially abundant peptides/proteins. Here, empirical Bayes moderated t-tests is applied, as implemented in the R/Bioconductor limma package (Smyth, 2004). The resulting per protein and condition comparison p-values are subsequently adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini-Hochberg method).

I included the input files and my script. Can you elaborate on this?

The input file is here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/186w3c-0r0u6kkYaA_aDwzkWZaRmxipjv/view?usp=sharing

Greets
Witek

messages.subject: Quantification function not correlating with groupcomparison results
messages.subject_clean: Quantification function not correlating with groupcomparison results
messages.body_plain:
Hello MSStats developers,

I don't know if here is the best place to write about this or on Github. I'm following the tutorials of the recently streamed course (thank you very much) and I found something odd. I want to use the summarized version from MSStats to do my own statistical comparison, so I used the quantification function of MSStats (quantification(quant.maxquant, type="group")) using the data processed data (quant.maxquant). I used both the tutorial data from MaxQuant and my own data, and in both cases the group or sample values do not correlate with fold changes obtained in the comparison done with MSStats. I tried to look for proteins without any missing values, to avoid any imputation, as I thought that the subtraction, e.g. C2-C1 should give the same value as the log2FC. I don't know if in the linear model the fold change is calculated differently (e.g. weighted average) or something like this, but just the subtraction don't match.

Example using the MaxQuant tutorial files:

Protein:
D6VTK4
C2-C1 log2FC: 0.257765170

quantification results:

D6VTK4
Condition1 25.34412
Condition2 25.65922

25.65922-25.34412 = 0.3151

All values I have tried are somehow similar, (go on the same direction) but are not the same.

Could you give me a hint why this is happening?

Thanks for the great package,

Alejandro

messages.subject: Re: Quantification function not correlating with groupcomparison results
messages.subject_clean: Quantification function not correlating with groupcomparison results
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alejandro,

quantification function summarizes $RunlevelData. Help file for quantification function mentions how they are calculated.

?quantification

- Sample quantification : If there are no tech replicates per sample, it is the same as run summarization ($RunlevelData). If there are tech replicates or experimental replicates, sample quantification is median among run quantification.
- Group quantification : median among sample quantification.

Input for quantification is the output of dataProcess function, which performs up to run summarization (haven't fit the linear mixed model for group comparison). and It is a median-based calculation.
median of LogIntensities for Group=1 in $RunlevelData : 25.34412
median of Log Intensities for Group=2 in $RunlevelData : 25.65922
They are matched with quantification results.

Group comparison function uses the linear mixed model, which generates average-based log fold changes from run summarization.
mean of LogIntensities for Group=1 in $RunlevelData : 25.40747
mean of Log Intensities for Group=2 in $RunlevelData : 25.66524

25.66524 - 25.40747 = 0.25577652, which is the estimated log2FC in the output of group comparison.

Hope it can be helpful.

- Meena
